glmGamPoi[2]

Fit Gamma-Poisson Generalized Linear Models Reliably.

[!IMPORTANT] this repo is a fork of upstream glmGamPoi. it is specifically designed to optimize memory use and runtime, without sacrificing the library’s existing accuracy or features. more details regarding using the fork, its scope, and relevant modifications are discussed in fork.md.

Pronounciation: dʒi əl əm ɡam ˈpwɑ

The core design aims of glmGamPoi[2] are:

  • Fit Gamma-Poisson models on arbitrarily large or small datasets
  • Be faster and more memory efficient than alternative methods, such as DESeq2 or edgeR
  • Calculate exact or approximate results based on user preference
  • Support in-memory or on-disk data
  • Follow established conventions around tools for RNA-seq analysis
  • Present a simple user-interface
  • Avoid unnecessary dependencies
  • Make integration into other tools easy

Installation

You can build and install glmGamPoi2 from the automatically automatically built package archive published from the latest GitHub release.

This can be done using the pak (for installation) R package via the following snippet:

pak::pak("url::https://github.com/goeva-lab/glmGamPoi/releases/latest/download/glmGamPoi2.tar.gz")
Details regarding optimized build instructions

To build and install the package with the maximal level of optimizations enabled for your particular machine, the withr package can be used as follows:

shared_flags <- "-fuse-ld=lld -flto -ffat-lto-objects -fopenmp"
withr::with_makevars(assignment = "=", c(
    CXX17STD = "-std=c++17",
    CXX17FLAGS = sprintf("%s -O3 -march=native", shared_flags),
    LDFLAGS = sprintf("%s -L/usr/lib64/R/lib -Wl,-O2 -Wl,--sort-common -Wl,--as-needed -Wl,-z,relro -Wl,-z,now -Wl,-z,pack-relative-relocs", shared_flags)
), {
    pak::pak("url::https://github.com/goeva-lab/glmGamPoi/releases/latest/download/glmGamPoi2.tar.gz")
})

If you use this package in a scientific publication, please make sure to cite the original glmGamPoi publication:

glmGamPoi: Fitting Gamma-Poisson Generalized Linear Models on Single Cell Count Data
Constantin Ahlmann-Eltze, Wolfgang Huber
Bioinformatics; 2020-12-09; doi: https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa1009

Example

An example of library use can be seen below:

library(glmGamPoi2)

counts <- rnbinom(n = 10, mu = 5, size = 1/0.7)

# design = ~ 1 means that an intercept-only model is fit
fit <- glm_gp(counts, design = ~ 1)
